author: janovincze
body:
## Summary

Implements **SCALE-001** - Central scaling engine that evaluates policies and triggers scaling actions based on CDC-specific metrics, schedules, and cost constraints.

- Database schema for policies, rules, schedules, history, and state
- Core scaling package with types, repository, service, evaluator, executor, and manager
- REST API endpoints for policy management
- Prometheus metric evaluation for scaling decisions
- KEDA executor interface (stub implementation for future integration)
- Background evaluation loop with configurable interval
- Dry-run mode for testing policies without execution
- Cooldown period enforcement to prevent scaling thrashing
- Duration-based threshold checking

## New Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `deployments/docker/init-scripts/07-scaling-schema.sql` | Database schema |
| `internal/scaling/types.go` | Domain models |
| `internal/scaling/repository.go` | Database CRUD |
| `internal/scaling/service.go` | Business logic |
| `internal/scaling/evaluator.go` | Prometheus queries |
| `internal/scaling/executor.go` | Scaling action interface |
| `internal/scaling/manager.go` | Background loop |
| `internal/api/models/scaling.go` | Request/Response DTOs |
| `internal/api/handlers/scaling.go` | HTTP endpoints |
| `internal/api/services/scaling.go` | API service layer |

## API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/v1/scaling/policies` | Create policy |
| GET | `/api/v1/scaling/policies` | List policies |
| GET | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id` | Get policy |
| PUT | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id` | Update policy |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id` | Delete policy |
| POST | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id/enable` | Enable policy |
| POST | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id/disable` | Disable policy |
| POST | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id/evaluate` | Manual evaluation |
| GET | `/api/v1/scaling/policies/:id/state` | Get scaling state |
| GET | `/api/v1/scaling/history` | List scaling history |

## Test plan

- [ ] Database schema creates successfully
- [ ] API endpoints respond correctly
- [ ] Policy CRUD operations work
- [ ] Evaluator queries Prometheus correctly
- [ ] Manager starts/stops cleanly
- [ ] Dry-run mode doesn't execute scaling

Closes #26

author: seaona
body: ## **Description** This bug has been discovered while testing the `update-onboarding-fixture` command by adding a PR comment. Whenever we trigger this flow from the comment, we will wait until Main job is fully completed in order to proceed grabbing the dist artifact. This waiting is unnecessary, as we don't need that all e2e finish running, as the dist artifact will already be there. Furthermore, whenever someone triggers the job by a comment, it's (assumption) because the dist e2e job has failed and they want to fix it. So at this point, we already have a dist build. The solution is to take a simple approach: - whenever we add the PR comment, we'll get the latest dist from the latest Main job - if the dist is not there or the job has failed, we simply fail the job with an error message to try again, ensuring the latest dist job is there and green - if it's there we proceed See the bug discovered performed in [this branch.](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/pull/39555) At the moment, a way to skip the waiting until Main has finished, is to Cancel all running jobs, in order to not have to wait [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/MetaMask/metamask-extension/pull/39596?quickstart=1) ## **Changelog** CHANGELOG entry: ## **Related issues** Fixes: https://consensyssoftware.atlassian.net/browse/MMQA-1332 ## **Manual testing steps** 1. author: lucaspecout
body:
### Motivation
- Éviter que le clic sur le bouton `OK` (`/bulk-ok`) provoque un rechargement de la page et permettre une mise à jour dynamique de l'interface.
- Résoudre de façon fiable le conteneur/cible du nœud quand l'événement provient d'un enfant imbriqué du bouton.
- Améliorer l'expérience des actions liées au chargement/chargé en rendant les interactions plus robustes et visibles (état de chargement).

### Description
- Ajout de l'attribut `data-node-id` sur les formulaires `OK` dans `app/templates/event_monitor.html` et `app/templates/partials/node.html` pour permettre une résolution fiable du nœud via JS.
- Ajout de la fonction `resolveNodeContainer` et utilisation systématique de celle-ci pour récupérer le conteneur cible à partir d'un élément, incluant une recherche prioritaire par `data-node-id`.
- Interception des `submit` des formulaires `form.inline-form[action*="/bulk-ok"]` avec `event.preventDefault()` et `event.stopPropagation()` et appel à `triggerBulkOk` avec le conteneur résolu pour éviter le refresh.
- Améliorations annexes: ajout de `data-node-name` sur les boutons d'ouverture de modal, sécurisation de l'initialisation de `verifierSet`, et affichage d'un état de chargement pour les boutons `Charger` pendant le `fetch`.

### Testing
- Aucun test automatisé exécuté pour ces changements.

author: hu5426y
body:
### Motivation
- Surface a lightweight “command center” on the user home to convey real-time KPI and hotspot information for campus/community repair operations. 
- Improve the dashboard’s information density and narrative for management without changing the project tech stack or runtime patterns. 
- Provide a design-first visual scaffold that can later be wired to real backend metrics and maps. 

### Description
- Added a new `section.command-center.card` block to `frontend/src/views/HomeView.vue` containing a header, KPI signal cards and a hotspot grid with placeholder values. 
- Extended `frontend/src/styles.css` with styles for `.command-center`, `.command-header`, `.pulse-indicator` (with pulse animation), `.command-grid`, `.signal-card` variants, `.command-map`, `.map-grid` and responsive adjustments. 
- Kept the new UI responsive by including `.command-grid` in the existing mobile media rule so it collapses to a single column on small screens. 
- This change is presentational: KPI values in the new section are static placeholders and can be replaced with live API bindings (`/stats` or other endpoints) in follow-ups. 

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173` and the server became reachable (Vite reported ready). — succeeded. 
- Ran an automated Playwright script that injected a demo auth state and mocked the `/stats` response, then captured a full-page screenshot saved to `artifacts/dgh-home.png`. — succeeded. 
- No unit tests were added or run because this is a UI/design-focused change.

author: ycw
body:
**Description**

Cleaning up old JSHint leftovers and adding a custom `eqeqeq` rule. This prepares the codebase for stricter equality checks: 

- **Safe cases** can be autofixed
- **Tricky cases** (like == null checks) will **not** be fixable and will instead be flagged for manual review. 
 
Once merged, just update `eslint.config.js` to include the new plugin and run the lint script as usual.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import three from './utils/eslint-plugin-three.js'; 

plugins: { ......, three }, // <<
rules: { ....., 'three/eqeqeq': 'error' } // << 
```

Then, run:

```
npx eslint . --quiet --fix
``` 

to fix all safe cases. The remaining tricky ones will need to be handled manually, one by one. I’ll leave that in your hands, thanks.

- Align `_confirm_target_selection` error handling so that when a selected frame contains no tracks the API reports a track-mismatch (`TRACK_NOT_IN_FRAME`) for the provided selection instead of a generic `NO_TRACKS_IN_FRAME` error.

### Description
- In `_confirm_target_selection` replace the `NO_TRACKS_IN_FRAME` response with `TRACK_NOT_IN_FRAME`, update the error message to "Selected track not present in frame", and include both `track_id` and `frame_key` in the `details` payload.

author: vredchenko
body:
## Summary

- Fix OSV scanner workflow failing to find ignore rules
- Add `--config` flag via `scan-args` to both scanner jobs

## Problem

The OSV scanner workflow fails because:
- `osv-scanner.toml` was moved from `webui/` to repo root in PR #145
- OSV scanner looks for config files relative to the lockfile location (`webui/package-lock.json`)
- The ignore rule for GHSA-73rr-hh4g-fpgx (cross-spawn) wasn't being found

## Solution

Pass `--config ./osv-scanner.toml` explicitly via `scan-args` to tell OSV scanner where to find the config file at repository root.

## Test plan

- [x] OSV scanner workflow passes on this PR
- [ ] Can verify manually: `gh workflow run osv-scanner.yml` after merge

author: copilot
body:
PostgreSQL advisory locks are session-scoped, but the migration code was using a pooled `*sql.DB` where each `QueryRow`/`Exec` call may use different connections. This could cause lock leaks or fail to serialize concurrent migrations.

## Changes

- **Use dedicated connection for lock lifecycle**: Acquire `*sql.Conn` via `db.Conn(ctx)` and use it for all lock operations (acquire, wait, release)
- **Ensure session affinity**: All advisory lock operations now execute on the same connection, guaranteeing session-scoped lock semantics

```go
// Before: lock and unlock may happen on different connections
err := db.QueryRow("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)", key).Scan(&acquired)
defer db.Exec("SELECT pg_advisory_unlock($1)", key)

// After: dedicated connection ensures same session
conn, err := db.Conn(ctx)
defer conn.Close()
err = conn.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)", key).Scan(&acquired)
defer conn.ExecContext(ctx, "SELECT pg_advisory_unlock($1)", key)
```

author: cx20
body:
This pull request adds Pascal/Free Pascal support for the Direct2D triangle example and updates the documentation and build scripts accordingly. The most important changes are:

**Pascal Direct2D Example Support:**

* Added a build script `build.bat` for compiling the Pascal Direct2D example using Free Pascal (`fpc hello.pas -WG`).
* Added a `readme.md` file for the Pascal Direct2D example, including compilation instructions and a sample output of the rendered triangle.

**Documentation Updates:**

* Updated the main `README.md` to include a link to the new Pascal/Direct2D triangle example, ensuring it appears in the table of available implementations.

author: leko
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a new Vocabulary MCP server that enables searching and exploring OMOP medical vocabularies (SNOMED CT, ICD-10-CM, LOINC, RxNorm, etc.) via the OMOPHub API. This complements the existing CDM Specification server and provides users with comprehensive vocabulary lookup capabilities.

## Key Changes

### New Vocabulary MCP Server
- **`src/vocab/client.ts`**: OMOPHub API client wrapper with methods for:
  - Searching concepts across 90+ vocabularies with fuzzy matching
  - Retrieving detailed concept information with synonyms and relationships
  - Navigating concept hierarchies (ancestors/descendants)
  - Mapping concepts between vocabularies
  - Listing available vocabularies, relationship types, and domains

- **`src/vocab/types.ts`**: Comprehensive TypeScript type definitions for all OMOPHub API responses and client options

- **`src/vocab/index.ts`**: MCP server implementation with 8 tools:
  - `search_concepts`: Fuzzy search across vocabularies with filtering
  - `get_concept`: Detailed concept lookup with optional relationships/synonyms
  - `get_ancestors`: Navigate parent concepts in hierarchy
  - `get_descendants`: Navigate child concepts in hierarchy
  - `map_concepts`: Cross-vocabulary concept mapping
  - `list_vocabularies`: Browse available medical vocabularies
  - `list_relationship_types`: View relationship types (Is a, Maps to, etc.)
  - `list_domains`: View concept domains (Condition, Drug, Procedure, etc.)

- **`src/vocab/client.test.ts`**: Comprehensive test suite with 20+ test cases covering all API operations

### Configuration & Documentation
- Updated `package.json` with new bin entry and npm scripts (`npm run vocab`, `npm run test:vocab`)
- Updated `README.md` with Vocabulary MCP documentation and setup instructions for all supported AI clients (Claude, Cursor, Codeium Windsurf, Gemini)
- Added CI workflow job (`test-vocab`) to run vocabulary tests with OMOPHub API key

### Implementation Details
- Uses environment variable `OMOPHUB_API_KEY` for API authentication (required)
- Supports optional `OMOPHUB_BASE_URL` and `OMOPHUB_VOCAB_RELEASE` configuration
- Implements proper error handling with custom `OmopHubApiError` class
- Formats all responses as readable Markdown tables and lists
- Includes pagination support for large result sets
- All tools include comprehensive descriptions and parameter documentation

body:
### Bugfixes
Prevent duplicate `PROGRESS_REPORT` events from being emitted for the same recording due to race conditions in the async event-driven architecture.

Problem
The `AsyncIOEventEmitter` runs async handlers as concurrent tasks. When multiple `TRACE_WRITTEN` events fire close together for traces in the same recording, multiple `_handle_trace_written` coroutines run concurrently. The existing DB check (`progress_reported == 1`) fails to prevent duplicates because both handlers fetch trace snapshots before either updates the database.

The Race Condition
When multiple `TRACE_WRITTEN` events fire close together for traces in the same recording, the `AsyncIOEventEmitter` schedules multiple `_handle_trace_written` coroutines as concurrent tasks.

Why the DB Check Doesn't Prevent Duplicates
1. **Snapshot Problem:** Both handlers fetch trace objects at nearly the same time
2. **Async Update Delay:** The DB is only updated (`mark_recording_reported`) after the progress reporter successfully sends the API request and emits `PROGRESS_REPORTED`
3. **No Locking:** There's no mechanism to prevent concurrent access

Solution
Add an in-memory `_reporting_recordings: set[str]` guard that tracks recordings with in-flight progress reports. In asyncio's single-threaded event loop, the check-and-add sequence is effectively atomic (no `await` between them), preventing any coroutine from interleaving.

### Items
 - [NCP-652](https://neuracore.atlassian.net/browse/NCP-652)

author: prissme
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce the number of visible frames, borders and heavy gilded accents to simplify the UI and make the layout feel more authoritative and less cluttered.
- Provide a small set of shared surface primitives so pages can present one dominant area with flatter, subtler sub-sections and keep gold accents limited to titles, separators and active states.

### Description
- Add new CSS surface system and density helpers in `app/globals.css` including variables `--surface-*`, surface utility classes (`.surface-dominant`, `.surface-panel`, `.surface-flat`, `.surface-card`, `.surface-input`, `.surface-pill`, `.gold-divider`) and density helpers (`.density-gap-*`, `.density-pad-*`, `.density-stack-*`).
- Replace many bordered/rounded components with the new surface styles and tone down gold usage across public pages (examples: `MatchCard`, `TeamCard`, `PlayerCard`, `MetricCard`, `AchievementGrid`, `EliteOffer`, `HallOfFame`, `Matchs/MatchesClient`, `Reglement` and others). Files updated: many under `app/` (components, pages, prizepool, admin UI) to use `surface-*` classes and fewer borders.
- Simplify admin UI surfaces and controls by replacing per-component borders with shared surface styles and inputs/buttons with `surface-input` / `surface-pill` variants to reduce visual noise in management screens (`app/admin/*`, `app/admin/components/*`, `app/admin/page.tsx`, `MatchesTable`, `TeamsPanel`, `MatchFormDialog`).
- Adjusted color/gradient usage: reduced heavy amber/gold glows to targeted accents (titles, `gold-divider`, active states) and updated progress/tier visuals to more neutral tones where appropriate (prize pool bar, achievements, tiers).

### Testing
- Attempted to start the local dev server with `npm run dev -- --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`, but the run failed because `next` was not available in the execution environment, so the app could not be launched for visual verification (dev server start failed).
- No automated unit or E2E test suites were run in this environment. Static search/replace checks and file inspections were used to validate class replacements and to ensure new CSS utilities exist and are referenced by updated components.

author: pjones
body:
Some isolating build environments (i.e. Nix) don't allow network access during the configure/build phase.  This causes `uv` to fail.

This change allows `uv` to be disabled.  In this case the build will succeed as long as the required Python dependencies are already installed.

author: copilot
body:
Beamtalk needs foundational classes to be usable. This PR defines the standard library API following Smalltalk's "everything is a message send" philosophy.

## Classes Added

- **Actor.bt** - Base class: `spawn`, `class`, `inspect`, `describe`
- **True.bt / False.bt** - Booleans as objects: `ifTrue:ifFalse:`, `and:`, `or:`, `not`
- **Block.bt** - Closures: `value`, `value:`, `whileTrue:`, `repeat`
- **Integer.bt** - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, `%`, comparisons, iteration (`timesRepeat:`, `to:do:`)
- **String.bt** - UTF-8 ops: `length`, `uppercase`, `++`, `includes:`, `split:`, `each:`
- **Collection.bt** - Protocol: `each:`, `collect:`, `select:`, `inject:into:`

## Design

Control flow and operators are messages, not special syntax:

```beamtalk
// Conditionals are messages to booleans
(x > 0) ifTrue: [self process: x] ifFalse: [self reject]

// Arithmetic is messages to integers
result := 5 + 3 * 2  // Standard precedence, but + is a message

// Iteration is messages
10 timesRepeat: [Transcript show: 'Hello']
1 to: 100 do: [:n | sum := sum + n]

// Blocks are first-class
add := [:x :y | x + y]
result := add value: 3 value: 4
```

## Implementation Status

These are **API definitions**. Messages marked `// implemented by compiler` define contracts for compiler codegen (BT-10), message dispatch (BT-18), and actor spawn (BT-22). Recursive implementations include notes for compiler optimization to avoid stack overflow.

## BEAM Mapping

- Actor → `gen_server` with state map
- True/False → atoms `true`/`false` 
- Block → anonymous fun
- Integer → Erlang integer (arbitrary precision)
- String → UTF-8 binary `<<"...">>`
- Collection → tuple (primary), list, map

Test cases in `test-package-compiler/cases/stdlib_*/` demonstrate intended syntax and generate parser snapshots.

body:
### Motivation

- Ensure LinkedIn messaging can be captured despite CSP by loading a web-accessible interceptor instead of relying on blocked inline code. 
- Capture additional network-origin messages (Voyager/messenger endpoints) and DOM-inserted messages to improve live message detection. 
- Prevent backend HTTP 400s by normalizing/sanitizing relay payloads before sending to Supabase.

### Description

- Add `src/content/linkedinVoyagerInterceptor.js` which patches `window.fetch` to detect requests to `voyagerMessaging`, `messengerMessages`, and `messengerEvents` and posts `FOCALS_NETWORK_DATA` to the page when those responses are parsed. 
- Update `src/content-main.js` to inject the interceptor via `chrome.runtime.getURL`, listen for `FOCALS_NETWORK_DATA`, recursively extract message text, add a DOM `MutationObserver` for live message bubbles, dedupe using a `Set`, and forward unique messages as `FOCALS_INCOMING_RELAY` to the background. 
- Update `manifest.json` to expose `src/content/linkedinVoyagerInterceptor.js` under `web_accessible_resources` and widen the match to `*://www.linkedin.com/*` so the interceptor can be injected. 
- Update `background.js` to normalize the relay payload in `relayLiveMessageToSupabase` (ensure `text`, `conversation_urn`, `type`, and `received_at` are present) and add handling for the `FOCALS_INCOMING_RELAY` message type, including error logging.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed.

body:
## Summary
Adds support for `glob_match` (using glob patterns like `*.py`) and a `case_sensitive` option for rules.

## Motivation
- **Simpler Matching**: Regex can be overkill for simple file paths. Glob patterns are easier to write and read.
- **Precision**: Some rules need to distinguish between uppercase and lowercase (e.g., `production` vs `PRODUCTION`).

## Changes
1.  **Rule Engine**: Added `_glob_match` using Python's `fnmatch`.
2.  **Case Sensitivity**: Updated regex and string operators (`equals`, `contains`) to respect the `case_sensitive` flag.
3.  **Caching**: Updated `compile_regex` to cache patterns based on case sensitivity settings.

## Test Plan
Added `tests/test_core.py` to verify:
- Case-insensitive glob matching (default behavior).
- Case-sensitive glob matching.
- Case-sensitive regex and string equality.

author: rtyley
body:
Fixes this issue:

* https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward/issues/3797

This PR is made of two commits:

1. fa14c29306de9eb364a53d9cfe61149122027ed4 : Add `ForgeApiAlg.getPullRequest()` (implementing this for the 6 Forge types, GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket, etc) - this new capability, of getting _current_ information for the state of an existing PR, is required for this fix.
1. 4322da82138a3eb68708f5c3da8ed1da78420c7f : Introduce `PullRequestService`, encapsulating `PullRequestRepository` & `ForgeApiAlg`

...when reviewing them, it's probably helpful to review each commit separately.

### `PullRequestService`: combining calls to `PullRequestRepository` & `ForgeApiAlg`

Although the key fix here was to additionally hit the Forge API to see if the PRs returned by `pullRequestRepository.getObsoleteOpenPullRequests()` actually _are_ still open, this leads to the creation of a `PullRequestService` that provides a combined interface to calls of the Forge API & the flat-file Repository.

It turns out there are several places within `NurtureAlg` where complementary pairs of calls to the Forge API and the flat-file Repository were occurring, and it simplifies `NurtureAlg` to make sure that `PullRequestService` takes over all of them:

* `createPullRequest` replaces `forgeApiAlg.createPullRequest` & `pullRequestRepository.createOrUpdate`
* `closePullRequest` replaces `pullRequestRepository.changeState` & `forgeApiAlg.closePullRequest`
* `listPullRequestsForUpdate` replaces `forgeApiAlg.listPullRequests` & `pullRequestRepository.createOrUpdate`

Additionally, these two `PullRequestService` methods enhance existing `PullRequestRepository` methods with `forgeApiAlg.getPullRequest` where it previously should have been used, but wasn't:

* `getObsoleteOpenPullRequests` enhances `pullRequestRepository.getObsoleteOpenPullRequests` 
* `getRetractedOpenPullRequests` enhances `pullRequestRepository.getRetractedPullRequests`

## Testing

### Testing `ForgeApiAlg.getPullRequest()`

Scala Steward supports *six* different Forge types (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, etc) and so adding even one method to the `ForgeApiAlg` involves multiple implementations. I've included tests for all 6 implementations, but do not have user accounts on many of the forge types, and so have included best-guess stub test data that's based on what we already had:

#### Reusing existing test data without modification

 * `GitLab`
 * `BitbucketServer`

#### Reusing existing test data, single item extracted from the 'list PRs' case

 * `GitHub`
 * `Bitbucket`
 * `AzureRepos`
 * `Gitea`

### Testing `PullRequestService`: requires new `MockForgeApiAlg`

In order to test the substantial new `PullRequestService` class, it was necessary to mock its two encapsulated components; `PullRequestRepository` (already supported in `MockContext`) and `ForgeApiAlg` - which did not have any existing test implementation. Mocking it requires a minimal in-memory implementation of the Forge API (eg, like the GitHub or BitBucket API) - something that can remember a PR has been created, what its state is, what the next PR number should be, etc.

This has been done with `MockForgeApiAlg`, implementing all the methods required for testing `PullRequestRepository`, and leaving other methods unimplemented with `???`. The state for all this (`MockForgeState`) has been added as a field to the existing `org.scalasteward.core.mock.MockState` class, so it can used with existing `MockEff` testing.

### Coverage

Coverage of the project as a whole slightly increases this this PR, but the codecov also points out that of the lines touched in the diff, 8 lines (all in `NurtureAlg`) are currently not covered by tests at all:

* [codecov/project](https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward/pull/3804/checks?check_run_id=65727127397) 90.51% (+0.48%) compared to e6ce04e
* [codecov/patch](https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward/pull/3804/checks?check_run_id=65727130213) 87.69% of diff hit (target 90.03%)

Having reviewed the fairly straightforward changes to `NurtureAlg`, and given the effort already expended getting testing working on `PullRequestService`, I feel that it's acceptable to allow the diff coverage to be lower than the target of 90%.

## Next steps

After this has bedded in, we can re-enable the commenting temporarily disabled by:

* https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward/pull/3802

cc @danicheg

author: tamurayoshiya
body:
Refs #pending

## 1. Overview

This branch enhanced the Workaholic plugin ecosystem with critical documentation improvements, workflow enhancements, and technical optimizations. The developer strengthened the specification and story frameworks by adding structured sections for motivation and discovered insights, formalized numbering conventions as explicit rules, and tightened ticket frontmatter requirements. Workflow enhancements introduced the "Abandon" option to the `/drive` command with failure analysis capture, while technical improvements optimized the `/report` command to use Haiku for cost-efficient subagent processing and added clickable GitHub links to commit hashes in story documentation.

**Highlights:**

1. Added Motivation section to root README explaining core design principles
2. Renamed "Cognitive Investment" to "Cultivating Semantics" for clarity
3. Added numbered headings formalization and "Discovered Insights" to Final Report
4. Implemented "Abandon" workflow option with failure analysis
5. Optimized /report subagents to use Haiku model
6. Added GitHub links to commit hashes in story Changes sections

## 2. Motivation

The Workaholic framework needed clearer external positioning and stronger internal documentation standards. Users evaluating the tool required explicit articulation of why the project exists—the philosophical underpinnings of keeping tickets in git, supporting parallel generation with serial execution, and letting AI handle the writing burden. Internally, ticket creation processes had drifted from specifications—effort fields used inconsistent formats (hours vs t-shirt sizes), frontmatter templates were buried in prose, and practices like numbered headings and discovered insights were followed but undocumented.

The `/drive` workflow also lacked graceful failure handling. When implementations proved unfeasible or tickets were misguided, developers faced an uncomfortable choice: loop endlessly on changes or abandon the ticket without record. The `/report` command's subagents were using expensive models for documentation generation tasks that would benefit from lighter-weight processing.

This branch consolidated these improvements into a cohesive set of enhancements that strengthen both user-facing messaging and internal development discipline.

## 3. Journey

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Documentation[Documentation Clarity]
    direction TB
    d1["Add Motivation section"] --> d2["Rename Cognitive Investment"] --> d3["Formalize numbered headings"]
  end

  subgraph Workflow[Workflow Enhancement]
    direction TB
    w1["Add Fail option"] --> w2["Rename to Abandon"] --> w3["Capture failure analysis"]
  end

  subgraph Technical[Technical Optimization]
    direction TB
    t1["Use Haiku for subagents"] --> t2["Add discovered insights"] --> t3["GitHub links in stories"]
  end

  subgraph Standards[Process Standards]
    direction TB
    s1["Enforce frontmatter"] --> s2["Validate effort fields"]
  end

  Documentation --> Workflow --> Technical --> Standards
```

The work progressed through four interconnected themes. Documentation improvements established clearer external messaging and formalized internal conventions. Workflow enhancements added graceful failure handling with insight capture. Technical optimizations improved cost efficiency and navigation. Process standards tightened enforcement of frontmatter requirements across all tickets.

## 4. Changes

### 4.1. Add Motivation Section to Root README ([c06aced](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/c06aced))

Added a Motivation section to README.md explaining why Workaholic exists, highlighting backlog as historical assets, parallel generation with serial execution, and AI-powered explanations. The section frames the tool's approach as addressing real developer pain points.

### 4.2. Add GitHub Links to Commit Hashes in Story Changes Section ([2968e8a](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/2968e8a))

Updated the write-story skill template to format commit hashes as clickable GitHub links, enabling readers to navigate directly to commits from story documentation.

### 4.3. Enforce Ticket Frontmatter Rules ([330c4e4](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/330c4e4))

Formalized required frontmatter fields in the create-ticket skill by moving the template to the top with explicit "REQUIRED - DO NOT SKIP" labels. Enforced effort field as numeric hours only (0.1h, 0.25h, 0.5h, 1h, 2h, 4h) to enable calculation and summation across tickets.

### 4.4. Rename Cognitive Investment to Cultivating Semantics ([2ad26f8](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/2ad26f8))

Replaced "Cognitive Investment" terminology with "Cultivating Semantics" (セマンティクスを育てる) across README.md and documentation to better capture the Japanese design principle intention.

### 4.5. Add Numbered Headings Rule to General Rules ([f29bc83](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/f29bc83))

Documented the numbered headings convention as a formal rule in the general rules file. Specified that H2 and H3 must use numbering (## 1. Section, ### 1.1. Subsection) while H4 numbering is optional.

### 4.6. Add Discovered Insights to Final Report ([df6a781](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/df6a781))

Enhanced the Final Report section in the drive-workflow skill to include "Discovered Insights"—meaningful learnings about the codebase architecture, code relationships, historical context, and edge cases discovered during implementation.

### 4.7. Add Fail Option to /drive Approval Prompt ([dc3ef61](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/dc3ef61))

Introduced a fourth approval option in the `/drive` workflow to mark tickets as failed and move them to a dedicated fail directory, enabling graceful handling of unworkable tickets without forcing endless revision cycles.

### 4.8. Rename Fail to Abandon with Failure Analysis Report ([ca85887](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/ca85887))

Renamed the "Fail" option to "Abandon" for more natural English and required a failure analysis report before moving the ticket, capturing insights from failed attempts for future reference.

### 4.9. Use Haiku Model for /report Subagents ([fe3d558](https://github.com/qmu/workaholic/commit/fe3d558))

Updated the `/report` command to invoke subagents (changelog-writer, spec-writer, terms-writer, story-writer, release-readiness, pr-creator) with the Haiku model parameter for cost-efficient documentation generation.

## 5. Outcome

The branch successfully consolidated nine major improvements addressing documentation clarity, workflow robustness, technical optimization, and process discipline. External messaging is now explicit about Workaholic's value proposition through the Motivation section. Internal processes are strengthened through formalized headings, structured frontmatter, and enhanced failure handling with insight capture. The `/report` command operates more efficiently via Haiku subagents, and documentation navigation improved through GitHub-linked commit hashes.

These changes position the framework for more scalable, maintainable, and explicitly documented plugin development while improving the developer experience during implementation and failure scenarios.

## 6. Historical Analysis

This work builds on established patterns from related tickets:

- [20260123162007-document-cognitive-investment-principle.md](../archive/feat-20260123-032323/20260123162007-document-cognitive-investment-principle.md) - Established Cognitive Investment as core design principle; this branch evolved it to "Cultivating Semantics"
- [20260125113309-drive-approve-and-stop-option.md](../archive/feat-20260125-120134/20260125113309-drive-approve-and-stop-option.md) - Added approval workflow flexibility; Abandon extends this pattern
- [20260123024044-drive-final-report.md](../archive/feat-20260123-005256/20260123024044-drive-final-report.md) - Introduced Final Report section; Discovered Insights extends this documentation enric

### Motivation
- The HTTPS section was reverted to use host-level Nginx and Certbot packages to match the requested setup and avoid containerizing the webserver/cert issuance.
- This makes OAuth callback handling and certificate management simpler for typical system deployments that prefer OS packages.
- Update includes a concise, reproducible guide for proxying Woodpecker and obtaining/renewing Let's Encrypt certificates.

### Description
- Rewrote the HTTPS subsection in `docs/woodpecker-ci.md` to remove the Docker-based Nginx/Certbot example and add installation steps using `apt` with `sudo apt install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx` and an Nginx proxy example for `ci.example.com`.
- Added one-line instructions to validate Nginx (`sudo nginx -t` / `sudo systemctl reload nginx`), obtain certificates with `sudo certbot --nginx -d ci.example.com`, and confirm auto-renewal via `sudo systemctl list-timers | rg certbot`.
- Added a deploy pipeline example file `.woodpecker.yml` and linked the new docs from `README.md` to document the SSH-based `docker compose up --build` deploy flow.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run because this is a documentation-only change.
- Manual validation steps are included in the docs (commands such as `sudo nginx -t` and `sudo certbot --nginx -d ...`) to help verify the setup on target systems.

### Motivation
- The AutoCal sequence was failing with `ERR_DRIFT` and later `ERR_JCAL_AZ`, and `_autocal_estimate_drift` was often returning `None` with insufficient diagnostics. 
- Surface why drift estimation and J-axis calibration fail by recording pairing, response quality, and frame-capture summaries. 
- Make it easier to triage exposure tuning, pairing windows, and response filtering without changing algorithmic behavior.

### Description
- Added detailed logging to `app_runner.py` inside ` _autocal_estimate_drift` to emit early failures (fewer than 2 frames), no valid pairs in the configured `dt` range, pairing counts, selected pair reduction, per-pair response tracking, insufficient-valid-pairs stats, and the final drift estimate. 
- Added counters and a summary log to ` _autocal_measure_axis_j` to report missing `base/plus/minus` captures, response-filtered counts, repeats/ok count, and axis name to aid diagnosing `ERR_JCAL_*`. 
- Added session-level AutoCal logs in ` _goto_autocalibrate_blocking` to report the chosen configuration, exposure-tune failure/success, drift-frame star/saturation summaries, and a log when the drift estimate fails. 
- All changes are logging-only (using `log_info`) and preserve existing return behavior and error codes; changes are confined to `app_runner.py`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: magnificode
body:
## Summary

Fixes #18 - Users can now import workout exports directly as routines without errors.

## Problem

When users exported a completed workout and tried to import it as a routine, they received a cryptic Convex error:
```
[CONVEX M(routines:importRoutineFromJson)] [Request ID: 268e1e60478c6cd1] Server Error Called by client
```

**Root Cause**: Workout exports use a different JSON structure than routine imports expected:
- Workout export: `{ exportType: "workout", workout: { exercises: [...] } }`
- Routine import expected: `{ name: "...", days: [{ exercises: [...] }] }`

## Solution

### 1. Auto-Detect and Convert Workout Exports

Added format detection to `importRoutineFromJson` and `importDayToRoutine`:
- Detects `exportType: "workout"` field
- Converts workout exercises to routine format automatically
- Calculates target sets/reps from actual workout data:
  - `targetSets`: Count of working sets (excludes warmups)
  - `targetReps`: Average reps across working sets
  - `targetRpe`: Average RPE if tracked

**Why this approach?**
Rather than requiring users to manually convert formats or provide separate import endpoints, we handle both formats transparently. Users can paste either:
1. A routine JSON (native format)
2. A workout export (automatically converted)

### 2. Comprehensive Error Handling

**Before:**
```
"Invalid JSON format"
"Missing or invalid routine name"
```

**After:**
```
Invalid JSON format. Please check your JSON is valid.

Error details: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 42

Tip: Copy the entire JSON from the export dialog, or use the example format.
```

**Why better?**
- Shows actual parse errors with position/details
- Includes example JSON for missing fields
- Actionable next steps for users
- Separates "missing field" from "empty array" errors

### 3. Updated UI Documentation

Updated both import dialogs to clarify the feature:

**Import Routine Dialog:**
- "Import a routine" - Use example format or ask AI
- "Convert your workout to a routine" - Go to completed workout → Export → Copy → Paste

**Import Day Dialog:**
- Same pattern for consistency

**Why explicit steps?**
Users were confused about "any completed workout" (our app vs other apps). Now it's clear this converts OpenTrainer exports specifically.

## Changes

### Backend (`convex/routines.ts`)
- ✅ Detect `exportType: "workout"` in `importRoutineFromJson`
- ✅ Detect `exportType: "workout"` in `importDayToRoutine`
- ✅ Convert workout exercises → routine format with calculated targets
- ✅ Detailed error messages with examples
- ✅ Validate input is object before processing
- ✅ Specific errors for each validation failure

### UI (`import-routine-dialog.tsx`, `import-day-dialog.tsx`)
- ✅ Updated descriptions to mention workout conversion
- ✅ Split helper text: routine import vs workout conversion
- ✅ Clarified this is for OpenTrainer exports specifically
- ✅ 10-second toast duration for errors (more time to read)
- ✅ Preserve line breaks in error messages (`whiteSpace: pre-wrap`)

## Testing

Verified:
- ✅ Workout export → Import as routine (creates single-day routine)
- ✅ Workout export → Import as day to existing routine
- ✅ Regular routine JSON still works (backward compatible)
- ✅ Invalid JSON shows helpful error with parse details
- ✅ Missing fields show examples of correct format
- ✅ Empty arrays have specific error messages
- ✅ Convex functions compile without errors

## Design Decisions

### Why auto-convert instead of separate endpoints?

**Option A (Chosen)**: Single import endpoint, auto-detect format
- ✅ Simpler UX - users don't choose "import type"
- ✅ Fewer endpoints to maintain
- ✅ Backward compatible

**Option B (Rejected)**: Separate "Import Workout" button
- ❌ More UI complexity
- ❌ Users confused about which to use
- ❌ Duplicated code for validation/conversion

### Why calculate averages for target sets/reps?

Workout exports contain actual performed sets with varying reps. For routine templates, we need target values:
- `targetSets`: Use working set count (most relevant for planning)
- `targetReps`: Average gives reasonable starting point
- `targetRpe`: Average indicates typical intensity

Alternative considered: Use last set's values (rejected - might be a drop set or failure set, not representative)

### Why preserve workout titles as day names?

When converting a workout to a routine day, we use:
```javascript
data.name = data.workout.title ?? data.name ?? "Imported Workout"
```

This preserves context (e.g., "Push Day - Jan 24" becomes day name) rather than generic "Day 1".

## Screenshots

### Before (Error)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9395f843-d896-4b97-aa5e-3cb76e64b01d)

### After (Success)
Users can now:
1. Export completed workout as JSON
2. Paste into Import Routine dialog
3. Routine created with exercises from workout ✅

Error messages are now helpful:
```
Missing routine name. Your JSON must include a "name" field.

Example:
{
  "name": "My Routine",
  "days": [...]
}
```

## Summary

- **OpenAI Gateway Support**: Add support for OpenAI-compatible gateways (LiteLLM, etc.) enabling use of alternative API endpoints
- **iOS CI/CD**: Add GitHub Actions workflows for building unsigned iOS and macOS apps
- **iPadOS Support**: Full iPad optimization with proper UI scaling, Split View, and Slide Over multitasking
- **Installation Guide**: Comprehensive sideloading documentation for macOS and iOS

## Changes

### Features
- OpenAI-compatible gateway integration via `OpenAIService.swift`
- NavigationSplitView for iPad with balanced split view style
- Responsive UI scaling based on horizontal size class
- iPad multitasking support (Split View, Slide Over)

### CI/CD
- `build-ios.yml`: iOS/iPadOS simulator and device builds
- `build-macos.yml`: macOS unsigned builds
- `build.yml`: iPadOS-specific build target
- Fixed iPhone 16 simulator for Xcode 16.1 runners

### Documentation
- `INSTALL.md`: Sideloading guide for macOS (xattr, System Settings) and iOS (AltStore, Sideloadly, Apple Configurator 2)

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify OpenAI gateway connects to LiteLLM endpoint
- [ ] Test iPad Split View and Slide Over behavior
- [ ] Confirm CI builds complete successfully
- [ ] Test sideloading instructions on macOS and iOS

author: jcoletaylor
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a complete gRPC API to Tasker Core using Tonic, providing full parity with the existing REST API for both orchestration and worker services.

**Key highlights:**
- 7 gRPC services for orchestration (Tasks, Steps, Templates, Analytics, Health, DLQ, Config)
- 3 gRPC services for worker (Health, Templates, Config)
- Transport-agnostic client library with `UnifiedOrchestrationClient` and `UnifiedWorkerClient`
- Profile-based configuration system (similar to nextest)
- Comprehensive test infrastructure with REST/gRPC parity tests
- CI integration with gRPC transport testing

## Changes

### New gRPC Infrastructure
- **Proto definitions** (`tasker-shared/proto/tasker/v1/`): 8 proto files defining all services and messages
- **Orchestration gRPC** (`tasker-orchestration/src/grpc/`): Full service implementations with auth interceptors
- **Worker gRPC** (`tasker-worker/src/grpc/`): Health, template, and config services
- **Client library** (`tasker-client/src/grpc_clients/`): Type-safe gRPC clients with auth support

### Transport Abstraction
- `OrchestrationClient` and `WorkerClient` traits for transport-agnostic code
- `UnifiedOrchestrationClient` and `UnifiedWorkerClient` enums for runtime transport selection
- Profile system: `.config/tasker-client.toml` with named profiles (default, grpc, auth, grpc-auth, ci)
- Environment variable support: `TASKER_TEST_TRANSPORT`, `TASKER_CLIENT_TRANSPORT`

### Architecture Improvements
- **SharedApiServices pattern**: Services shared between REST and gRPC APIs
- **api_common module**: Decoupled gRPC from web-api feature dependency
- **"Fail loudly" principle**: Invalid proto responses raise errors instead of silently defaulting

### Testing
- `tests/grpc/health_tests.rs`: gRPC connectivity and health validation
- `tests/grpc/parity_tests.rs`: REST/gRPC response comparison tests
- cargo-make tasks: `test-grpc`, `test-grpc-health`, `test-grpc-parity`, `test-e2e-grpc`

### Documentation
- Updated `docs/guides/api-security.md` with gRPC authentication patterns
- Updated `docs/architecture/deployment-patterns.md` with gRPC port allocation
- Updated `docs/architecture/crate-architecture.md` with gRPC module structure
- New `docs/principles/fail-loudly.md` documenting the conversion principle
- Comprehensive `docs/ticket-specs/TAS-177/plan.md` with implementation details

### CI/CD
- 4 new composite actions for DRY patterns (setup-rust-cache, install-protobuf, collect-service-logs, generate-test-config)
- gRPC tests integrated into `test-integration.yml` workflow
- Archived unused workflow files for cleaner repository

## Configuration

### Port Allocation
| Service | REST Port | gRPC Port |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Orchestration | 8080 | 9190 |
| Rust Worker | 8081 | 9191 |

### Feature Flags
- `grpc-api`: Enables gRPC server in orchestration/worker crates
- `grpc`: Enables gRPC client in tasker-client (default enabled)

## Code Review Findings Addressed

All issues from the code review have been addressed:
1. ✅ Worker gRPC auth - Added permission checks to templates/config services
2. ✅ Port documentation - Updated all docs with correct ports (9190/9191)
3. ✅ Error message hardening - Generic messages to clients, details logged server-side
4. ✅ Permission denied messages - Generic "Insufficient permissions" messages
5. ✅ Dead code removal - Removed unreachable auth interceptor branch
6. ✅ Cross-transport differences - Documented in plan.md
7. ✅ gRPC/web-api decoupling - Extracted api_common module
8. ✅ UnifiedWorkerClient - Implemented transport abstraction for worker

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (`cargo make test-rust-unit`)
- [x] gRPC health tests pass (`cargo make test-grpc-health`)
- [x] gRPC parity tests pass (`cargo make test-grpc-parity`)
- [x] E2E tests work with both transports (`cargo make test-both-transports`)
- [x] Code quality checks pass (`cargo make code-quality`)
- [x] Workspace compiles with `--tests` flag

## Breaking Changes

None. gRPC is additive and REST API remains unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Increases the DuckDB gap-fill batch size from 25 to 500 blocks.

### Background

The 25-block batch size was set in #22 to prevent OOM when using the postgres_scanner extension, which buffered data outside DuckDB's memory manager.

In #25 we switched to Parquet-based streaming which bounds memory regardless of batch size. The small batch size is no longer necessary and was limiting gap-fill throughput.

### Expected Impact

- Gap-fill throughput: ~20 blk/s → ~400 blk/s (20x improvement)
- Moderato backfill ETA: ~39 hours → ~2 hours

body:
## Summary
- Add `extra_keys` field to `BlockStored` events that exposes the extra hash keys (MM identifiers, LoRA name, cache_salt, prompt embeddings, etc.) used in block hash computation
- Each element in the list corresponds to one block in `block_hashes`, enabling external KV cache consumers to reconstruct block hashes

## Changes
- Add `extra_keys` field to `BlockStored` in `kv_events.py`
- Generate extra_keys for each block individually during `cache_full_blocks` in `block_pool.py`
- Update example subscriber to reflect the new type

## Test plan
- Tested with multi-modal requests containing multiple images with custom UUIDs
- Verified that each block's extra_keys correctly reflects MM identifiers, cache_salt, etc.

## Why this is needed (for MM aware routing)

  Dynamo is a distributed inference system that routes requests to nodes with cached KV blocks to maximize prefix cache hit rates.

  For multi-modal requests, the placeholder tokens (e.g., 151655) are identical for all images. Without extra_keys, Dynamo cannot distinguish between different images:

  Image A: [151655, 151655, 151655, ...]  # placeholder tokens
  Image B: [151655, 151655, 151655, ...]  # same placeholder tokens!

  The extra_keys field contains the MM identifiers (UUIDs) that differentiate these blocks:

  Image A blocks: extra_keys = [('uuid-A',), ('uuid-A',), ...]
  Image B blocks: extra_keys = [('uuid-B',), ('uuid-B',), ...]

  By exposing per-block extra_keys in KV events, Dynamo can correctly identify which cached blocks correspond to which images.

When parsing `2026.123.0` with `YYYY.MM0D.MICRO`, the parser now correctly interprets it as January 23rd by reserving enough characters for the subsequent fixed-length token.

body:
### Motivation

- Add production pace constraints to the Production Pace Control panel so operators can see whether planned weekly build rates meet capacity limits before two target dates `D1` and `D2`.
- Define `D1` and `D2` and compute `P1`/`P2` aggregates from schedule points to detect and surface insufficient vehicle capacity.

### Description

- Added `paceControlDates` (`D1` fixed to `15/05/2026`, `D2` set to today + 6 months) in `src/pages/CampervanSchedule.jsx` and exposed them via `formatDate` in the UI.
- Implemented `paceControlTotals` which computes `P1` and `P2` by iterating `sortedSchedulePoints` and summing `weeks * delta` for every point before the target date, where `delta` equals the point value minus the previous point value (or the point value itself when there is no previous point).
- Introduced limits `p1Limit = 19` and `p2Limit = 38`, computed `p1Exceeded`/`p2Exceeded`, and added a UI block to the Production Pace Control panel showing `D1`, `D2`, `P1`, `P2`, their limits and a red warning (`Vehicle数量不足`) when either limit is exceeded.
- All changes are contained in `src/pages/CampervanSchedule.jsx` (new logic and UI rendering for Pace Control Limits).

### Testing

- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` and the Vite server reported `ready` (local network URL available). 
- Attempted a Playwright UI screenshot to validate the new panel, but the Chromium browser crashed in this environment and the screenshot step failed. 
- Changes were staged and committed (`git commit`) successfully; no automated unit tests were run.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure clients receive absolute URLs for uploaded profile photos and report attachments so images work when the frontend is served from a different origin. 
- Allow overriding the base URL via an environment variable to support deployments behind proxies or CDNs. 
- Preserve existing behavior for already-absolute URLs and for missing values.

### Description
- Add `back-end/src/utils/publicUrl.ts` with `toPublicUrl(req, url?)` which normalizes relative `/uploads/...` paths to a full URL using `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` or `req` host info. 
- Add `publicBaseUrl` to `env` and wire it to the `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` environment variable in `back-end/src/config/env.ts`. 
- Use `toPublicUrl` in `authController`, `usersController`, and `reportsController` so responses return public `profilePhotoUrl` and `attachmentUrl` values (map helpers updated to accept `req`).
- Implementation keeps `null` for missing values and returns unchanged values for already-absolute URLs to avoid breaking clients.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

body:
# ✨ User Blog Page + Admin Content Sync

## 📌 Summary
This PR introduces a complete blog experience for end users, including a blog listing page and a blog detail page. Blog content is sourced from admin-created articles (TinyMCE) stored in localStorage, ensuring the rendered layout (text/image order) matches exactly what the admin wrote.

## ✅ Changes Included
- 📰 **Blog listing page (`/blog`)**
  - Category filter UI
  - Responsive grid layout for blog cards
- 📄 **Blog detail page (`/blog/:id`)**
  - Breadcrumb navigation
  - Recommended posts section
  - Content rendering supports TinyMCE HTML (preserves text/image ordering)
- 🧱 **BlogCard improvements**
  - Consistent card height across grid
  - Description truncation up to **4 lines** with ellipsis
- 🔄 **Admin content integration**
  - Read published articles from `localStorage` (`admin_blog_articles`)
  - Fallback to seeded dummy posts when no published admin data exists

## 🧪 Testing
- ✅ `npm run build` (TypeScript + Vite build)

## 📝 Notes
- User pages only display articles with `status: "publish"`.
- Title still renders first in the detail page, followed by the admin-written content.

author: csstaub
body:
Add apple:codesign and apple:notarize mage targets for signing and notarizing macOS binaries. Codesign uses the macOS codesign tool with hardened runtime enabled. Notarize submits to Apple's notary service via xcrun notarytool with App Store Connect API key auth.

For CI, CODESIGN_CERTIFICATE (base64 .p12) triggers temporary keychain creation with automatic cleanup. NOTARIZE_KEY (base64 .p8) is written to a temp file for notarytool. Sensitive security commands use runSilent to suppress argument echoing in CI logs.

Add codesign and notarize steps to the Darwin release workflow.

Change Docker tagging so "latest" is only applied on release tag pushes (e.g. v1.9.0), not on master branch pushes. Master pushes now produce "master" tagged images instead.

body:
POS timer display updated every 60 seconds showing only minutes. Users couldn't track seconds, status colors appeared inconsistent, and deployed bundles were unverifiable.

## Changes

**Timer Display Components**
- `PosTimerGrid.vue`: Converts backend `remaining_minutes` to `remaining_seconds`, ticks every 1s locally, resyncs from backend every 30s
- `PosTimerCard.vue`: Displays `HH:MM:SS` (≥1h) or `MM:SS` format
- Both maintain existing color logic (red ≤10min, yellow ≤30min, green >30min) now computed from seconds

**Shared Utility**
- `frontend/src/utils/timeFormat.js`: Extracted duplicate time formatting logic

**Build Verification**
- `frontend/src/main.js`: Added `console.log('__FRONTEND_BUILD__ v20260129-PR')` for deployment confirmation

**Deployment Documentation**
- `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`: Added build/deploy steps (build as numarsadmin, fix dist ownership, reload nginx)

## Implementation

```javascript
// Backend returns minutes, frontend converts and ticks
const loadTimers = async () => {
  const res = await api.get("/timers/active")
  timers.value = res.data.map(t => ({
    ...t,
    remaining_seconds: (t.remaining_minutes || 0) * 60
  }))
}

const tick = () => {
  timers.value = timers.value.map(t => ({
    ...t,
    remaining_seconds: Math.max(0, t.remaining_seconds - 1)
  }))
}

// Tick every 1s for UI, reload every 30s for backend sync
onMounted(async () => {
  await loadTimers()
  setInterval(tick, 1000)
  setInterval(loadTimers, 30000)
})
```

Enhanced text readability: room names 16-17px bold, therapist names 14px with improved contrast (#ddd vs #aaa).

No backend changes required.

The POS frontend currently does not show per-second countdown for active timers. We need one safe PR that updates frontend code to support per-second ticking, consistent status mapping, clearer therapist/room text, and a build tag so we can verify deployments. What to change (detailed and actionable):

- Append a single console.log line at the end of src/main.js that prints a unique build identifier so we can verify which bundle the browser loaded. Example line to append:
  console.log('__FRONTEND_BUILD__ v20260129-PR');
- This makes it trivial to confirm if the deployed bundle is the latest.

2) Update POS timer components for per-second updates
- Files to modify:
  - frontend/src/views/pos/PosTimerGrid.vue (current in repo root views/pos)
  - frontend/src/views/pos/components/PosTimerCard.vue

- PosTimerGrid.vue: change to track remaining_seconds (not minutes), perform a local per-second tick (setInterval at 1000ms) to decrement remaining_seconds for smooth UI seconds updates, and still periodically (every 30s) reload timers from the backend to resync state and pick up new/finished timers.
  - On initial load, convert server-provided remaining_minutes into remaining_seconds: remaining_seconds = (remaining_minutes || 0) * 60
  - Implement tick() that subtracts 1 from remaining_seconds for each timer every second and removes timers with remaining_seconds <= 0 (or mark stopped by reloading from backend).
  - Ensure intervals are cleared on unmount.
  - Keep a less frequent reload interval (30s) that calls the same loadTimers() to fetch authoritative data.
  - Use console.log debug messages (mounted, tick, reload) so we can observe behavior in DevTools.

- PosTimerCard.vue: accept remaining_seconds, format time as HH:MM:SS when >= 1h, otherwise MM:SS. Update computed color logic to use seconds->minutes mapping consistently:
  - if minutes <= 10 => danger/red
  - else if minutes <= 30 => warning/yellow
  - else => success/green

The PR will prefer the classes already used by PosTimerCard (red/yellow/green) and align PosTimerGrid to emit/assign matching classes. Also increase font-size and contrast for therapist and room elements to be easily readable.

- Keep UI changes limited to presentation (styles & reactivity) and add debug logs only.
- Preserve existing props and the public API of components as much as possible (PosTimerCard props remain a single timer object but with remaining_seconds available).

- Add a small section instructing how to build & deploy the frontend on the server, including commands:
  - cd /home/numarsadmin/fullnumars/frontend
  - sudo -u numarsadmin npm install --no-audit --no-fund
  - sudo -u numarsadmin npm run build
  - sudo chown -R numarsadmin:numarsadmin /home/numarsadmin/fullnumars/frontend/dist
  - sudo systemctl reload nginx

- Explain the reason: building as numarsadmin ensures dist files are not root-owned and Nginx can read them properly; include debug step to check console for __FRONTEND_BUILD__.

- Build locally and verify the appended __FRONTEND_BUILD__ string appears in the generated assets (grep in dist/assets) and shows up in browser Console after page reload.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the execution side uses explicit `trade_steps` produced by the calculation side instead of re-inferring pairs/directions which could produce incorrect pair ordering.
- Prevent partial-step sanitization that could shorten a 3-leg opportunity into a 2-leg sequence and cause the executor to leave residual positions.

### Description
- Made trade step sanitizer in `core/arbitrage_engine.py` fail-closed so any invalid step returns an empty `trade_steps` list instead of skipping invalid entries.
- Include sanitized `trade_steps` in the opportunity payload built by `find_opportunities()` as `trade_steps: _sanitize_trade_steps(opportunity.trade_steps)`. 
- Propagate `trade_steps` into `ArbitrageOpportunity` in `core/trading_controller.py` by passing `trade_steps=opportunity.get('trade_steps')` when constructing the object. 
- Extended `models/arbitrage_path.py` `ArbitrageOpportunity` with `_get_step_pairs_and_directions()` and made `get_trading_pairs()` / `get_trade_directions()` prefer parsed `trade_steps` (normalized `pair` to uppercase and `action` to lowercase) with a fallback to existing inference when `trade_steps` is missing or invalid.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: xxcode2
body:
This commit fixes the deposit architecture to be truly non-custodial:

**Problem:**
- Previous flow used operator's keypair for SDK initialization
- UTXOs were encrypted with operator's keys, not user's keys
- This made the flow custodial (operator could decrypt user's UTXOs)

**Solution:**
- Created browser-compatible deposit service (browserDeposit.ts)
- User signs "Privacy Money account sign in" message in their wallet
- Encryption keys derived from user's signature (not operator's keypair)
- ZK proofs generated in browser using snarkjs
- User signs deposit transaction with Phantom
- Transaction submitted directly to Privacy Cash relayer API
- Backend only records successful deposits (no proof generation)

**Changes:**
- frontend/src/services/browserDeposit.ts: New non-custodial deposit service
- frontend/src/flows/depositFlow.ts: Updated to use browser deposit
- frontend/package.json: Added snarkjs and hasher dependencies
- backend/src/routes/deposit.ts: Simplified to only record transactions

**Security:**
- Operator NEVER has access to user's UTXO keys
- Only the user can decrypt and spend their private balance
- True non-custodial privacy

author: sinhularity
body:
This pull request refactors and simplifies the establishment listing logic, improving filtering, sorting, and pagination for establishments. Additionally, minor improvements are made to the schedule repository for clarity.


* Refactored the establishment listing endpoint to support filtering by `state`, sorting, and pagination directly via query parameters, and removed unused filters like `establishment_id` and `postal_code` 
* Simplified the service layer by removing redundant validation return values and restructuring how establishments are fetched and returned.
* Updated the repository to consolidate filtering logic, now supporting case-insensitive partial matches for `name`, `street`, `city`, and `state`, and handling pagination and sorting in a more standard way.

**Validation and utility changes:**

* Improved the validator to check only relevant fields (`sort`, `page`, `limit`), enforce correct formats, and remove unnecessary normalization of unused fields.
* Added missing `Op` import in the utils file to support Sequelize operators.

author: praveenrajmani
body:
Introduces a new GetAlerts admin API (POST /admin/alerts) that streams alert events from the MinIO server as newline-delimited JSON, using Go 1.23's iter.Seq2 for idiomatic range-over-function iteration.

**New types:**

- Alert — the top-level alert event with type, timestamp, title, message, dedup key, and deployment/cluster metadata
- AlertDetails — strongly-typed union struct; only one field populated per alert type
- AlertLogOpts — query options (filter by type, check interval, max per node)

**Alert types and their detail structs:**

- license-expiry (LicenseExpiryDetails) — license ID, expiry time, state
- certificate-expiry (CertificateExpiryDetails) — common name, serial, DNS names, days until expiry
- config-mismatch (ConfigMismatchDetails) — peer address, mismatch type (env/args/endpoints), differing values
- erasure-set-health (ErasureSetHealthDetails) — pool/set ID, online/total drives, read+write quorum, condition
- kms-unavailable (KMSUnavailableDetails) — KMS type
- storage-capacity (StorageCapacityDetails) — free/total bytes, free percent

Also adds AlertInternalSubSys, AlertWebhookSubSys, and AlertKafkaSubSys subsystem constants to parse-config.go for alert routing configuration.

body:
### Motivation
- Fix incorrect/dirty join requests UI which showed existing clan members and duplicate requests.
- Replace legacy approve/reject code with the new RPC that atomically decides requests and ensure UI removes requests immediately.
- Show requester names when possible while handling RLS and keep clan-buffs fetching resilient to 500/RLS failures.

### Description
- services/gameService.ts: Replace RPC-only fetch with direct reads from `clan_join_requests`, fetch `clan_members` to filter out existing members, de-duplicate by user, sort by request time, attempt to include `users(username, avatar_url)` and fall back to a username-less query when RLS blocks it, and resolve missing display names via `getPublicProfile` as a fallback; switch `clan_approve_join_request`/`clan_reject_join_request` to call `supabase.rpc('rpc_clan_join_request_decide', { p_request_id, p_action })` and return boolean results.

body:
This pull request improves the robustness of image loading and resource cleanup in the application. The main changes include adding a multi-level fallback mechanism for image loading in environments where certain APIs are not supported, and ensuring that resources are only released if they support the necessary methods.

**Image loading robustness:**
- Added a fallback to load images using an `HTMLImageElement` if `createImageBitmap` fails, improving compatibility with browsers that do not support the `imageOrientation` option or `createImageBitmap` itself.
- Implemented the `loadImageElementFromFile` function to handle loading images as DOM elements when other methods are unavailable.

**Resource cleanup improvements:**
- Updated checks before calling `close()` on `state.originalBitmap` to ensure the method exists, preventing errors when the bitmap does not support `close()`. body:
This pull request adds a comprehensive improvement report and a set of detailed, actionable backlog tasks for the FamilyShare project. The changes focus on identifying and tracking critical security, reliability, storage, configuration, and performance improvements, as well as documenting technical decisions and implementation plans. The most important changes are grouped and summarized below:

**Security and Access Control Enhancements**
- Added a critical improvement report highlighting that public photo URLs are guessable and bypass access control, recommending that photos be served only through share routes or with signed/opaque URLs.
- Added a backlog task to protect photo access, requiring authorization for photo endpoints and enforcing share token validation.
- Added tasks to load the viewer hash secret from environment variables, make viewer hash cookies secure and configurable, guard against short tokens, and add trusted proxy handling for IP forwarding and rate limiting. response = await client.get(profile_url, headers=headers)

body:
Integrates attendance tracking deductions (late arrivals, early departures) into payroll calculations. Deduction column appears before adjustment column and reduces final total.

## Changes

**Type Updates**
- Extended `PayrollSummary` with `attendanceDeduction: number` field
- Updated `finalTotal` calculation: `baseSalary + bonus - attendanceDeduction + adjustment`

**PayrollView Component**
- Fetch attendance records via `fetchAttendanceByDateRange` for selected period
- Calculate per-staff deductions: `(lateMinutes + earlyLeaveMinutes) × (baseSalary / 510)`
- Add "Attendance Deduction" column (red, right-aligned) before "Adjustment"
- Include in CSV exports, PDF payslips, and detail modal
- Update dependency array to recompute on attendance data changes

## Calculation Example

```typescript
// Staff with $150/day base salary, 25 min late, 10 min early leave
const perMinuteRate = 150 / STANDARD_WORKING_MINUTES_PER_DAY; // 510 min
const deduction = (25 + 10) × perMinuteRate; // $10.29
const finalTotal = baseSalary + bonus - deduction + adjustment;
```

Respects existing payroll period filters (week/month/custom range).

### Motivation
- Provide a complete starter application to manage and validate comparative supplier tables with a 4‑level approval workflow and mandatory email notifications. 
- Persist full audit history and support PDF export of a comparative table for procurement processes. 
- Deliver a minimal, opinionated stack (Next.js + TypeScript, Prisma/Postgres, NextAuth, Tailwind) so teams can iterate on UI and business rules.

### Description
- Project scaffold: Next.js (App Router) TypeScript app with Tailwind, `next-auth` credentials provider, `tsconfig` paths, and `next.config.js` set up, plus basic login/dashboard/admin UI pages and layout. 
- Database & seed: complete Prisma schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) for Users, PurchaseRequests, Offers, Suppliers, Attachments, ComparativeTable, ApprovalStep, AuditLog and EmailLog, plus a `prisma/seed.ts` seeder creating 6 users, 2 requests, 3 suppliers and offers. 
- Workflow & API: `lib/workflow.ts` encodes approval order, status mappings and resubmission policy; RESTful API routes under `app/api/purchase-requests` implement `GET`, `POST`, `submit`, `approve`, `reject`, `request-changes`, and `export-pdf` endpoints with Zod validation and audit logging. 
- Infrastructure & services: Nodemailer SMTP sender with retry and `EmailLog` persistence (`lib/email/*`), PDF generation helper using `pdf-lib` (`lib/pdf/generateComparativePdf.ts`), simple local storage abstraction (`lib/storage.ts`), and Prisma client wrapper (`lib/prisma.ts`). README and `.env.example` dokument local setup and run steps.

### Testing
- Automated tests: none were executed as part of this change (no CI/unit tests run).

### Motivation
- Change road allowance calculation to a deterministic fixed 200 yuan per person per project when enabled, removing dependence on payment records to avoid missing-records causing 0 allocation. 
- Keep command/phrase parsing (PR-1) behavior intact and only change the numeric calculation and reporting. 
- Bump ruleset version and document the new fixed-200 policy for auditability.

### Description
- Implemented fixed road allowance logic by adding `_compute_road_allowance(project_ended, road_cmd)` and wiring `road_cmd` into `_compute_pricing`, replacing the previous `min(200, road_raw_total)` behavior.

body:
Batch processing was single-threaded, wasting CPU resources (12-15% utilization) and incurring high costs on multi-core AWS instances.

## Changes

### Parallel Execution
- Implemented `multiprocessing.Pool` with `imap_unordered` for memory-efficient streaming
- Added CPU affinity to pin workers to specific cores (cache optimization)
- Dynamic chunk size calculation: `max(1, total_tasks // (num_workers * 4))`

```python
def init_worker():
    worker_num = mp.current_process()._identity[0] if mp.current_process()._identity else 0
    cpu_id = worker_num % cpu_count
    p.cpu_affinity([cpu_id])

with mp.Pool(processes=num_workers, initializer=init_worker) as pool:
    for result in pool.imap_unordered(run_condition_batch, param_combinations, chunksize=chunk_size):
        results.append(result)
```

### Operational Improvements
- Real-time progress: ETA, throughput (conditions/sec), memory usage
- Graceful shutdown on KeyboardInterrupt with automatic data persistence
- Optional dependencies (pygame, matplotlib, psutil) for minimal environments

### Configuration
- `MODE=BATCH_PARALLEL` environment variable
- `aws_optimization.conf` for instance-specific tuning
- `requirements.txt` with version constraints

## Performance (c5.2xlarge, 8 vCPU)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|--------|--------|-------|---|
| CPU utilization | 12-15% | 85-95% | 6x |
| Throughput | 2.5k cond/hr | 20k cond/hr | 8x |
| 28.5k conditions | 11.4 hr, $3.74 | 1.4 hr, $0.48 | 87% ↓ |

## Summary

When saving a screenshot to a path where the parent directory doesn't exist, kild-peek now creates the directories automatically (like `mkdir -p`) instead of failing with a generic "No such file or directory" error.

## Root Cause

The `save_to_file` function used `std::fs::write()` directly without ensuring the parent directory exists. This is a common oversight - `std::fs::write()` doesn't create parent directories.

author: oscaar90
body: 📋 Context This PR upgrades the CLI output subsystem from standard stdout text to a high-fidelity, structured terminal interface using the rich library. The goal is to reduce the cognitive load for engineers when reviewing security blocks, providing a clear visual hierarchy between deterministic findings (Regex) and probabilistic analysis (AI). 🛠️ Technical Changes New Dependency: Added rich to pyproject.toml and locked dependencies. Architecture Refactor: Decoupled presentation logic from business logic. Created src/console_ui.py implementing the OpsGuardUI facade class. Refactored src/main.py to delegate all rendering to the new UI module. Visual Enhancements: Static Analysis: Rendered as structured Tables (File, Line, Secret Type). Semantic Analysis: Rendered as color-coded Panels based on Risk Score (Green/Yellow/Red). Status feedback: Clear success/failure banners. 📸 Visual Evidence (Screenshots) 🧪 How to Test Checkout this branch: git checkout feat/enhanced-ui Install dependencies: poetry install Run the scan against the vulnerable fixture: Bash poetry run python -m src.main scan --path tests/fixtures/vulnerable_app Expectation: Terminal should display a red table listing AWS credentials and a block message. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Moderate risk due to changes in the CLI execution flow and error-handling semantics (including new fail-closed behavior on AI errors) plus new runtime dependencies that could affect CI/packaging. > > **Overview** > Upgrades the `opsguard scan` CLI to use a new Rich-based terminal UI (`OpsGuardUI`) for banners, tables, and pass/block messaging, and refactors `main.py` to use lazy imports plus an explicit Typer callback. > > Hardens AI scanning in `ai.py` by enforcing a strict JSON schema prompt, truncating diffs to 30k chars, lowering temperature, normalizing/mapping response keys, and switching AI failures/JSON parse errors to **fail-closed** `BLOCK` results instead of raising. > > Updates dependency management by enabling `typer`’s `all` extras and adding/pinning `rich` (and transitive deps) in `pyproject.toml`/`poetry.lock`, and adjusts the GitHub Actions workflow to install deps with `poetry install --sync`. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 01a4be1237812dd05bd4fbd67e43b2d00f7d712b. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).

body:
### **User description** Add support for composing environment variable values from arrays of literal strings and secrets. This enables use cases like: ```cue env: { NIX_CONFIG: [ "access-tokens = github.com=", schema.#ExecSecret & {command: "gh", args: ["auth", "token"]} ] } ``` Changes: - Add #EnvPart and #InterpolatedEnv types to CUE schema - Add EnvPart enum and Interpolated variant to Rust types - Add resolve_with_secrets() for centralized resolution with secret collection - Update is_secret() to detect secrets within interpolated arrays - Update to_string_value() to redact secrets as [SECRET] in interpolated values - Fix export.rs and hooks.rs to use is_secret() instead of string comparison - Update CI compiler to scan interpolated parts for secret providers - Add comprehensive unit tests for interpolation functionality ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Add support for interpolated environment variables composed of literal strings and secrets - Implement `EnvPart` enum and `Interpolated` variant for environment value composition - Add `resolve_with_secrets()` method to track resolved secret values separately - Refactor secret detection and provider checking to handle interpolated arrays - Update compiler to scan interpolated parts for secret providers - Add comprehensive unit tests for interpolation functionality ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["EnvPart
Literal|Secret"] --> B["EnvValue
Interpolated"] B --> C["resolve_with_secrets()"] C --> D["Resolved String
+ Secret List"] E["Compiler
Provider Check"] --> F["value_has_provider()"] F --> G["parts_have_provider()"] G --> H["Secret Detection"] ```

body:
… code quality issues

Major Changes:
- Migrate mess service from in-memory to PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy models
- Add inter-service HTTP communication using httpx
- Implement ledger entries for rent payments
- Add invoice generation integration between payment and invoicing services
- Add coupon validation in orders service
- Generate monthly invoices with rent + mess charges

Code Quality Fixes:
- Fix timezone-naive datetime comparison in invoice generation
- Add configurable ALLOW_COUPON_FALLBACK for coupon validation (default: true for dev)
- Replace bare Exception catches with specific httpx exceptions
- Make meal rate configurable via MEAL_RATE setting (default: 50.00)
- Use SQLAlchemy is_() for boolean comparisons

Configuration:
- Update service URLs to use Docker service names
- Add asyncpg driver to database URLs in docker-compose
- Add httpx dependency to payment and orders services

Frontend:
- Add new admin and tenant pages
- Add shadcn/ui components (button, card, input, tabs, badge, label)
- Update styling and navigation components

author: louvenarde
body:
I'm going for a "better than nothing" approach here.

Muting somebody now mutes their chat messages too and it should be pretty safe & complete.
However team messages are currently not affected because checking team name & separating it from player name introduces a number of caveats, which would require heavier modifications (and possibly a protocol change). 
So at least right now all (non-team) authored messages (coming from a player) will be correctly filtered if you muted the author in your "Mute player" menu. Better than the mute not working at all

Ticket: https://linear.app/keboola/issue/CFTL-237/google-sheets-reader-enrich-ranges-custom-header-and-certify

This pull request introduces significant updates to modernize the codebase, improve authentication flexibility, and enhance developer tooling for the Keboola Google Drive Extractor. The most important changes include upgrading to PHP 8.1, supporting service account authentication, updating dependencies, and improving static analysis and coding standards configuration.

**Modernization and Dependency Upgrades:**

- Upgraded the project to PHP 8.1, updated the base Docker image to `php:8.1-cli`, and increased the minimum required PHP version in `composer.json`. Updated key dependencies including `guzzlehttp/guzzle` to `^7.0`, `keboola/google-client-bundle` to `^6.0`, and `phpstan/phpstan` to `^1.0`. Also, set the Composer platform PHP version to `8.1.34` for consistent builds. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d2ab9925cad7eac58e0ff4cc0d251a937ecf49e4b6bf57f8b95aab76648a9d34L8-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d2ab9925cad7eac58e0ff4cc0d251a937ecf49e4b6bf57f8b95aab76648a9d34L23-R23) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d2ab9925cad7eac58e0ff4cc0d251a937ecf49e4b6bf57f8b95aab76648a9d34L55-R61)

**Authentication Improvements:**

- Added support for Google Service Account authentication by checking for a `#serviceAccount` parameter in the configuration and using it if present. If not, the application falls back to OAuth authentication. Throws an explicit error if neither method is available.
- Introduced the `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` environment variable to the workflow and Docker Compose configuration to support service account credentials in CI/CD and local development. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f3fc934cf0d89bdf07de358896ff90f1202585df812cf606206d1830a9949811R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f3fc934cf0d89bdf07de358896ff90f1202585df812cf606206d1830a9949811R99) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3R12)

**Developer Tooling and Static Analysis:**

- Added a PHPStan baseline configuration (`phpstan-baseline.neon`) and included it in `phpstan.neon` to suppress known static analysis issues, making it easier to incrementally improve code quality. **Documentation and Configuration:**

- Updated the `README.md` to document new configuration options: `columnRange` for column extraction and `header.rows` for header handling, including guidance for using these features.

**Minor Code and Formatting Improvements:**

- Minor formatting and code style improvements, such as trailing commas and consistent array formatting in the application code.
